page: Microsoft Azure E8_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 system provides 8 virtual CPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio (1:8 ratio). The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystems. In synthetic and application benchmark evaluations, the E8_v5 demonstrates consistent middle-tier performance across central processing and memory subtests. It records a PassMark CPU score of 11,416.97, single-core Geekbench score of 1,637.0, and multi-core score of 6,072.0. Memory throughput reaches 59.7 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 43.2 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached small-block reads achieve 416.84 GB/sec.

System throughput scales solidly for caching and web serving, delivering 7.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.21 GB/sec in static web throughput. However, compute-bound compression and parallel execution reveal specific limitations: multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranks in the lower quartile at 31.95 GB/sec, and larger language model inference demonstrates weak throughput, achieving 7.51 tokens per second on 7B models. From an efficiency standpoint, the instance balances cost by pairing high memory capacity with standard enterprise compute density, making it best suited for relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise applications, and mid-sized data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E8_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for enterprise memory-bound tasks. It includes no bundled local disks or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate balanced mid-range performance, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,072.0, PassMark CPU rating of 11,416.97, and 7.91 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers 59.7 GB/sec for uncached read streams. While raw multi-threaded decompression and large model inferencing display lower efficiency, the dedicated core architecture and high memory density make the E8_v5 well suited for memory-intensive workloads including relational databases, Redis caching layers, and in-memory analytics.
